Root cause confirmed in source: SelectTcgen05Ld (NVPTXISelDAGToDAG.cpp:296-297) builds the offset target constant with MVT::i32 while the machine instruction operand is i64imm:$offset (NVPTXIntrinsics.td:5915) and the intrinsic operand is i64 — so the i32 width is a genuine inconsistency, not deliberate narrowing. getZExtValue() yields the full 64-bit value, and getTargetConstant(val, MVT::i32) constructs APInt(32, val, isSigned=false), tripping isUIntN(32,val) for any value >= 2^32. Control case with offset i64 2 compiles cleanly to "...16x32bx2.x2.b32 {%r2,%r3}, [%r1], 2;", isolating the failure to the >2^32 value. The fix MVT::i64 is correct and matches the instruction's own operand type; under NDEBUG the same root cause silently truncates the immediate to its low 32 bits (miscompile). Every refutation avenue (invalid IR, UB-only, non-repro, semantically-correct output) is closed. The only minor caveat is that real split offsets are tiny so this value is semantically meaningless, but that does not license a crash/truncation on valid verifier-accepted IR.
